description: Shared Neo N3 CreateContractHash test vectors (platform-contract-library-v2 sections 4.1 and 8). Consumed by BOTH contracts/__tests__/CreateContractHashVectorTests.cs (xunit, pins neo-core Helper.GetContractHash) and framework/test/aa-account-hash.test.ts (vitest, pins deriveAppAccountHash). The preimage script is: ABORT (0x38) || PUSHDATA1(sender as 20 little-endian bytes) || PUSHINT(nefChecksum, minimal signed little-endian NeoVM integer push) || PUSHDATA1(strict-UTF8 manifest name); the hash is ripemd160(sha256(script)) displayed big-endian with 0x prefix. The sender component is MEASURED transaction-sender semantics for contract-initiated deploys (PlatformRegistryHashSemanticsTests) — the registry row, not this derivation, is the address-of-record.

vectors.notes: The PlatformRegistryHashSemanticsTests in-engine measurement: TestEngine ValidatorsAddress as transaction sender, the committed contracts/build/DeployerProbeFixture.nef checksum, child manifest name DeployerProbeChild, observed post-deploy hash.
Checksum in the 0..16 range exercises the single-opcode PUSH7 integer encoding branch.
Checksum 100 exercises the PUSHINT8 single-byte encoding branch.

Checksum 0x00abcdef: the minimal little-endian bytes end with a high bit set, so the signed encoding appends a 0x00 sign byte and the value must STILL be classed as PUSHINT32 (width chosen after sign extension). Dropping the sign byte outright is caught by the >=0x80000000 vectors, which cross the PUSHINT32/PUSHINT64 width boundary.
Checksum 0xffffffff (max uint32) does not fit a signed 4-byte integer, so it takes the PUSHINT64 branch; the 64-char manifest name pins the registry's maximum appId length.
